page: Amazon Web Services i7i.metal-48xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 8559C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 320 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated matrix operations.

The server is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. For local storage, it bundles 45000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, designed for high-throughput and low-latency data access. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included in this hardware profile.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations. It demonstrates exceptional throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving. While single-core performance falls into the average category, multi-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression and software compilation leverage the massive core count to achieve top-tier results.

This hardware profile offers high resource density, combining massive local NVMe storage with extensive DDR5 memory. It is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring direct access to physical hardware without hypervisor overhead. The server is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, data-intensive ETL pipelines, and local LLM inference tasks.
